body.name: That
body.construction:
This definition gives the finite algorithms, with every tuning choice deterministic. Put \(D=[1/2,1]^d\), \(D_h=hD\), and let \(v_s\) be the vector of monomials through degree \(m_s=\lceil s\rceil-1\); write \(H_s=\int_Dv_s(z)v_s(z)^{\mathsf T}dz\), \(\lambda_s=\lambda_{\min}(H_s)\), and \(\mathcal F_s(M)=U\operatorname{diag}(\eta_j\vee\lambda_s/4)U^{\mathsf T}\) for a symmetric \(M=U\operatorname{diag}(\eta_j)U^{\mathsf T}\). For \(n<6\) both branches return \(0\). For \(\kappa>0\) (and as the all-\(\kappa\) first-order fallback), take \(h=n^{-1/(2t+d+\kappa)}\), \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}\), split the sample into consecutive near-equal blocks \(I_1,I_2,I_3\), and form on \(D_h\)
\[
 \widehat c_g=H_\alpha^{-1}\frac1{|I_1|}\sum_{i\in I_1}h^{-d}\mathbf1_{D_h}(X_i)v_\alpha(X_i/h)\frac{4A_i}{r_\kappa(X_i)},\quad \widehat g(x)=\Pi_{[1,2]}\{v_\alpha(x/h)^{\mathsf T}\widehat c_g\},\quad \widehat e(x)=r_\kappa(x)\widehat g(x)/4,
\]
\[
 \widehat G_0=\frac1{|I_2|}\sum_{i\in I_2}h^{-d}\mathbf1_{D_h}(X_i)(1-A_i)v_\beta(X_i/h)v_\beta(X_i/h)^{\mathsf T},\quad \widehat s_0=\frac1{|I_2|}\sum_{i\in I_2}h^{-d}\mathbf1_{D_h}(X_i)(1-A_i)v_\beta(X_i/h)Y_i,
\]
\[
 \widehat\mu_0(x)=\Pi_{[1/8,7/8]}\{v_\beta(x/h)^{\mathsf T}\mathcal F_\beta(\widehat G_0)^{-1}\widehat s_0\},\quad \widehat Q=\frac1{|I_3|}\sum_{i\in I_3}h^{-d}\mathbf1_{D_h}(X_i)\frac{A_i}{\widehat e(X_i)}v_\gamma(X_i/h)v_\gamma(X_i/h)^{\mathsf T},
\]
\[
 \widehat b=\frac1{|I_3|}\sum_{i\in I_3}h^{-d}\mathbf1_{D_h}(X_i)v_\gamma(X_i/h)\left\{\frac{A_i}{\widehat e(X_i)}-\frac{1-A_i}{1-\widehat e(X_i)}\right\}\{Y_i-\widehat\mu_0(X_i)\},\qquad \widehat\tau_n^{(1)}(0)=\Pi_{[-3/4,3/4]}\{v_\gamma(0)^{\mathsf T}\mathcal F_\gamma(\widehat Q)^{-1}\widehat b\}.
\]
The ratios are evaluated only on \(D_h\), where \(r_\kappa>0\); flooring, clipping, and the stated small-sample fallback make this a total Borel rule. For the bounded-overlap second-order branch \((\kappa=0)\), put \(S=\alpha+\beta\), \(S_\star=d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\), and \(D_\star=1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2S)\). Use \(h=n^{-1/(\gamma D_\star)}\), \(k=\lceil n^{(d/S-d/\gamma)/D_\star}\rceil\) when \(S<S_\star\), and \(h=n^{-1/(2\gamma+d)}\), \(k=\max\{1,\lceil nh^d\rceil\}\) when \(S\ge S_\star\). Let \(p=m_\gamma+\max\{m_\alpha,m_\beta\}\), choose the fixed sufficiently large integer \(M_0\), set \(M=M_0+\lfloor k^{1/d}\rfloor\), and use the explicit cellwise scaled tensor-Legendre basis \(b_k\) of degree at most \(p\) on the \(M^d\) equal cells of \([0,1]^d\). Its known Lebesgue Gram matrix is \(\Omega=\int b_kb_k^{\mathsf T}=I\). With a fixed Lebesgue-orthonormal polynomial vector \(v\) through degree \(m_\gamma\), define \(w_h(x)=h^{-d}\mathbf1\{x\in[0,h]^d\}\), \(v_h(x)=v(x/h)\mathbf1\{x\in[0,h]^d\}\), \(b_{h,k}(x)=b_k(x/h)\mathbf1\{x\in[0,h]^d\}\), and fixed pilots \(\bar e=3/8\), \(\bar\mu=1/2\). For \(o=(x,a,y)\), put \(\phi_{a1}=a(a-\bar e)\), \(\phi_{y1}=(y-\bar\mu)(a-\bar e)\), and for ordered pairs put \(\phi_{a2}(o_1,o_2)=-(a_1-\bar e)b_{h,k}(x_1)^{\mathsf T}\Omega^{-1}b_{h,k}(x_2)a_2\) and \(\phi_{y2}(o_1,o_2)=-(a_1-\bar e)b_{h,k}(x_1)^{\mathsf T}\Omega^{-1}b_{h,k}(x_2)(y_2-\bar\mu)\). Writing \(\mathbb P_n f=n^{-1}\sum_i f(O_i)\) and \(\mathbb U_nH=\{n(n-1)\}^{-1}\sum_{i\ne j}H(O_i,O_j)\), compute
\[
 \widetilde Q=\mathbb P_n[w_h(X)v_h(X)\phi_{a1}(O)v_h(X)^{\mathsf T}]+\mathbb U_n[w_h(X_1)w_h(X_2)v_h(X_1)\phi_{a2}(O_1,O_2)v_h(X_2)^{\mathsf T}],
\]
\[
 \widetilde R=\mathbb P_n[w_h(X)v_h(X)\phi_{y1}(O)]+\mathbb U_n[w_h(X_1)w_h(X_2)v_h(X_1)\phi_{y2}(O_1,O_2)].
\]
Choose the deterministic Borel singular-value decomposition \(\widetilde Q=U\operatorname{diag}(s_j)V^{\mathsf T}\) by lexicographic eigenspace tie-breaking, set \(\widetilde Q_{\rm fl}=U\operatorname{diag}(s_j\vee3/32)V^{\mathsf T}\), and output \(\widehat\tau_n^{(2)}(0)=\Pi_{[-3/4,3/4]}\{v(0)^{\mathsf T}\widetilde Q_{\rm fl}^{-1}\widetilde R\}\). Thus both procedures use only sample moments, known finite Lebesgue-Gram matrices, deterministic rank/bandwidth choices, finite matrix operations, flooring, and clipping on every dataset.
